items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: Bob Rosengarden was saying, he called them “Wilderisms” that you used to do on the Dick Cavett band?

ctx.x: he did that. He brought them in. So I took it home and it was Del Staigers , and he had a very high pitched voice “and now when you do this —” you do so and so and so and so. He had a voice like that. But his playing was really beautiful. And of course the recording wasn’t that great because of the time at which it was done. So I thought to myself, now what can I do to put Dick Perry on when I go back with these recordings? And I had one of these big LP’s on rubber about that thick, those old recordings, it was…
Yeah, I’ve learned that you’re quite a practical joker. Bob Rosengarden was saying, he called them “Wilderisms” that you used to do on the Dick Cavett band?

Oh yeah. I was always — you know the pages would ask the audience to write questions or some comment, make a comment about something. So he said, “why don’t you write something?” So I wrote a thing — I had been doing research on the Salem witch trials, and I discovered that during that period there were two sisters who were also burned at the stake — the Kendall sisters — and one was Mary and the other one was Susan Kendall. And it just turns out by coincidence that Mary Kendall was the first woman who burned at…
